draft.title: Hypothetical Memory Experiment: Context Length vs. VRAM Usage
draft.body:
This post outlines a hypothetical experiment to understand the relationship between context length and VRAM consumption in local LLMs. The core scenario is that a specific model, runtime, and hardware configuration are held constant throughout the tests. The objective is to observe memory usage at different context lengths without collecting any data on output quality or inference speed.

Specifically, the hypothetical data suggests that a context length of 2048 tokens might require approximately 7 GB of VRAM, while extending this to 8192 tokens could increase the requirement to around 11 GB. It's crucial to reiterate that these are purely hypothetical figures from a planned, not executed, experiment. No actual benchmarks or performance metrics were gathered.

This is intended to frame a discussion on resource planning for larger context windows. What are others' experiences with memory scaling, even if qualitative, when exploring longer contexts?

Conclude by inviting discussion on resource planning for context length, framed by the hypothetical data.

draft.title: Exploring Hypothetical VRAM Scaling with Increased Context Length
draft.body:
We are exploring a hypothetical scenario to investigate how VRAM requirements scale with increasing context length for local language models. The setup assumes a fixed model, runtime environment, and hardware configuration to isolate the impact of context size. No actual performance or quality metrics are being measured in this theoretical exercise.

The hypothetical data points suggest a significant increase in memory footprint as context length grows. For instance, a context of 2048 tokens is projected to use around 7 GB of VRAM, whereas a jump to 8192 tokens is hypothetically estimated to require approximately 11 GB. These numbers are strictly for illustrative purposes within this hypothetical framework and do not represent measured results.

This thought experiment aims to gauge community understanding of memory scaling. What factors typically influence VRAM usage when extending context length, beyond the raw token count? Are there common patterns observed when planning for longer contexts, even without specific benchmark data?
